reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about synthesis-structure-property relationships in noble metal HEAs, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behaviors of multi-component noble metal nanomaterials under varying synthesis temperatures.
premises: High-temperature synthesis ensures complete atomic mixing in noble metal HEAs
Complete atomic mixing yields a stable, single-phase alloy
Homogeneous phase optimizes adsorption of reaction intermediates
Lower-temperature synthesis leads to elemental clustering or phase segregation
Clustering/segregation disrupts active site ensembles and degrades performance
